title: Where k-means starts, it ends
hook: Same four points, same algorithm. Can the starting guess change the answer?

knows: that points can be grouped by closeness
doesNotKnow: how k-means groups points by repeating assign-and-move
that its result depends on the starting centres

misconception: Given the data, a grouping algorithm finds the one right grouping.
objective: The learner can explain that k-means only improves its current guess, so it can settle on a worse grouping from a bad start, and that it is usually run from several starts.

claims.text: Each k-means step assigns every point to its nearest centre, then moves each centre to the mean of its points.
claims.source: Bishop 2006, Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning, §9.1 (the two-stage k-means iteration). Toy conventions in Demo.tsx: ties go to centre 1; a centre with no points stays put.

claims.text: From centres 0 and 4 on points 0, 4, 6, 10: the first step gives groups {0} and {4, 6, 10} and moves the second centre to 6.67; then 4 is 2.67 from that centre and 4 from the other, so nothing changes again. Total squared distance 18.7.
claims.source: Assign: 0 → 0; 4, 6, 10 → 4. Means: 0 and 20/3 = 6.67. Reassign unchanged. Cost 0 + (4 - 6.67)² + (6 - 6.67)² + (10 - 6.67)² = 7.11 + 0.44 + 11.11 = 18.67. Reproduced by centresAfter/cost in Demo.tsx.

claims.text: The grouping {0, 4} and {6, 10} costs 16, and starting centres such as 2 and 8 reach it.
claims.source: Means 2 and 8: (0-2)² + (4-2)² + (6-8)² + (10-8)² = 16. From (2, 8): 0, 4 → 2; 6, 10 → 8; centres stay (2, 8). Reproduced by centresAfter/cost in Demo.tsx.

claims.text: k-means settles on a local, not necessarily the best, grouping, which is why it is usually run from several starts.
claims.source: Bishop 2006, §9.1 (convergence to a local minimum; multiple restarts); Arthur & Vassilvitskii 2007, 'k-means++: the advantages of careful seeding' (SODA).

recall.question: You run k-means twice on the same customer data and get two different groupings. What is the most likely reason?
options: The runs started from different centres and settled in different places
One run has a bug, since k-means has one right answer
recall.why: k-means only improves the grouping it starts from, so different starts can settle on different groupings. Compare their total distances and keep the best, or use several starts.
